item.title: Office Standup
item.description:
Office Standup #

Overview #

A meeting held standing up, in which all the teams working in the same workplace gather. The following are shared:

  • NewFaces (new members)
  • Interestings (things that are interesting or of interest)
  • Helps (things you are struggling with or want help with)
  • Events (today’s events)

Purpose #

Create a daily work rhythm together with the members working in the same workplace. It also provides an opportunity for communication beyond team boundaries.

item.title: Team Standup
item.description:
Team Standup #

Overview #

A meeting held standing up with all members of the team. The following are shared, and tasks are checked.

  • What I did yesterday
  • What I will do today
  • Learnings / things I am struggling with

Purpose #

Share the plans and progress of every team member’s tasks, detect issues early, and help one another as a team to move forward.

item.title: Pre-IPM
item.description:
Pre-IPM #

Overview #

Pre-IPM is a meeting in which draft user stories are reviewed from the Developer’s perspective in preparation for the IPM (Iteration Planning Meeting). It is held by the Product Manager, the Designer, and one pair of Developers.

Purpose #

Confirm that the user stories are sufficiently prepared for discussion and estimation at the IPM and for starting implementation.

Frequency and Timing #

  • Once a week, 30–60 minutes
  • Held regularly on a fixed day of the week to keep the team’s rhythm
  • If there are only a few target user stories, or they are unlikely to be revised based on Developer feedback, Pre-IPM and IPM are held together

How to Run It #

  • The Product Manager and Designer explain the user stories to be estimated at the IPM
  • The Developers review the user stories from the following perspectives
    • Is it expressed in a way that makes the value to the user understandable?
    • Is it feasible?
    • Is the story an appropriate size (does it need to be split)?
    • Is a SPIKE or investigation needed before implementing the user story?
  • If changes are needed, agree on how to revise them
  • (After the meeting) The Product Manager/Designer revise the user stories

Tips

  • Which Developers attend is decided based on skills, the type of user story, the status of ongoing work, and so on.

item.title: IPM
item.description:
IPM #

Overview #

The IPM (Iteration Planning Meeting) is a meeting in which we estimate each user story and plan the next iteration. The Product Manager leads the meeting, the Product Manager and Designer explain the value to be delivered, and all the Developers estimate together.

Purpose #

We share the content of the prioritized user stories so that the Developers can proceed with implementation. We also estimate the stories to forecast how many user stories can be completed in the iteration one to two weeks ahead.

item.title: CL Meeting
item.description:
CL Meeting #

Overview #

The CL meeting is a forum for sharing information with the CL (Client Liaison)/PMO.

Purpose #

By sharing information regularly, we build a cooperative relationship aimed at the success of the project.

Frequency and Timing #

  • Once a week, 30 minutes
  • Held at the end of the week (Friday)

How to Run It #

  • Updates from the agile team
    • Development progress
      • Quantitative assessment (points of completed stories, velocity)
      • Qualitative assessment
    • Work status and upcoming plans for each role
    • Issues and requests
  • Updates from the PMO
    • PMO work status and upcoming plans
    • Issues and requests

Tips

item.title: Retrospective
item.description:
Retrospective #

Overview #

The retrospective (retro) is an activity in which the team reflects on its activities. Members openly bring up what went well and what did not go well in the iteration, and decide on actions for improvement. It is held in a relaxed atmosphere over drinks.

Purpose #

Its purpose is to continuously improve the team’s process, and it is an important activity in agile development. The team aligns its understanding so that good things are continued and things that do not go well are improved, leading to better team performance. In addition, a sense of unity emerges as the team shares together what went well and what they struggled with, and thinks about how to deal with it.

item.title: Sales Sync Meeting
item.description:
Sales Sync Meeting #

Overview #

The sales sync meeting is a forum for sharing information with the sales team and other people who serve as points of contact for each end user. When necessary, the team also asks the sales team for help, such as with research.

Purpose #

By sharing information regularly, we build a cooperative relationship aimed at the success of the project. People who serve as points of contact for end users need accurate information about the timing and content of product releases, as well as the direction of the product. Also, hearing the voices of end users, even on topics the team has not researched directly, can lead to new discoveries and become the seeds of the next hypotheses.

item.title: Internal Sync
item.description:
Internal Sync #

Overview #

Internal Sync is a meeting held only among members from within the company. Members share what they learned from the day’s work, clear up open questions, and discuss future policies and ways of working.

Purpose #

When there are things that are hard to talk about in front of members from outside the company, this meeting provides psychological safety for sharing and consulting. It is also used as time to summarize learnings for internal reporting.

item.title: Risks & Mitigations
item.description:
Risks & Mitigations #

Overview #

The team lists the risks to achieving its goals and considers measures to mitigate them. Each person’s assumptions are made visible, prioritized based on impact, the team’s state of learning, and so on, and then addressed.

Purpose #

Identifying risks and considering countermeasures helps improve the team’s performance. By validating the various assumptions made visible through this activity, the team can carry out its ideas with confidence and move forward.

item.title: Feedback
item.description:
Feedback #

Overview #

Give candid evaluations of and points for improvement on another person’s behavior.

  • Do it on a flat basis, regardless of seniority or position.
  • Always give feedback one-on-one.

What to Give Feedback On #

  • Tell the other person things that will benefit them.
  • Adapt the content to the situation.
    • Strengths / room for growth
    • What is going well / what would be good to change
    • What to start / what to stop / what to continue

The Mindset Behind Feedback # 

How can I personally become a better team member?
How can we work better together?

Purpose #

We encourage growth by building on each person’s strengths and improving their weaknesses. This also leads to building a better team.

item.title: Ice Break
item.description:
Ice Break #

Overview #

The team steps away from development work and plays games and the like together.

Purpose #

The aim is to stimulate communication among members and to refresh both mind and body.

Frequency and Timing #

  • About once every two weeks
  • Held so that it does not take a large chunk of time away from development
  • If the team agrees, it can be held at any time: during working hours, lunch breaks, short breaks, or after hours

How to Run It #

  • Decide what to do
  • Decide when to do it
  • Have fun

Examples

  • Table tennis
  • Switch
  • Word Wolf [How to play]
  • Various board games
  • Finding-things-in-common game [How to play]
  • GeoGuessr (a game of guessing locations in Street View) [How to play]
  • Small talk

item.title: Team Health Check
item.description:
Team Health Check #

Overview #

The team conducts an anonymous survey to make the state of the team visible.

Purpose #

The purpose is to learn how members feel by sharing opinions based on the survey results, take the actions the team needs, and make it a better team.

Frequency and Timing #

  • About once every two weeks
  • When there is a change in the project situation (structure, schedule, etc.)

How to Run It #

  • Step 1: Create the survey items (owner: Product Manager)
    • Set items such as the following
      • Psychological safety: I can freely say and share what I think. I also get feedback from the team
      • Vision: The vision for the business, service, and product is clear, and everyone on the team understands it
      • Mission: Everyone on the team shares what we should accomplish and the direction we should aim for
      • Autonomy: Rather than just doing what we are told, the team can make decisions to some extent
      • Enablement: Even after the engagement ends, we can teach other teams what we learned
      • Risk: We can work without fear of failure
      • Users: We understand the users’ needs
      • Stakeholders: They support the team and the product (they are interested in it)
      • Continuous improvement: We are always improving based on feedback from users
      • Attitude toward work: Working as a team is fun
    • Set up answer options such as the following
      • Answer choices
        • Going well, nothing to add
        • There are obstacles, but we can overcome them
        • There are problems that may negatively affect the team
      • Optional comment field (reason when choosing “there are obstacles” or “there are problems”)
  • Step 2: Answer the survey (owner: core members)
  • Step 3: Tally the survey responses (owner: Product Manager)
  • Step 4: Share the results (owner: core members)

    • Look at the survey results and exchange opinions within the team

    • If something is not going well for some reason, identify the necessary action items

    • Sample results

item.title: 1on1
item.description:
1on1 #

Overview #

Team members talk with each other one-on-one. Rather than a career-oriented 1on1 between a manager and a direct report, this is a casual conversation with a teammate you work closely with.

Purpose #

Through 1on1s, members share what went well and what they are worried about, ask for advice on their concerns, and offer new insights.

Frequency and Timing #

  • 1–2 times a month, about 15–30 minutes
  • Held as needed according to the wishes and circumstances of the members, without being bound by a fixed frequency

How to Run It #

  • Schedule it while taking into account pair assignments and the work in progress
  • Secure a place where you can talk one-on-one, such as Zoom or a meeting space
  • Hold the 1on1 meeting and clear your mind

    Example topics

    • Small talk
    • Thoughts about the team
    • Recent concerns
    • How you want to grow through the project

item.title: Radio Taiso
item.description:
Radio Taiso #

Overview #

Radio Taiso is a set of calisthenics performed to musical accompaniment, devised to improve physical fitness and maintain and promote health.
In Japan, it is widely loved by the public as an exercise that anyone can enjoy casually.

Purpose #

By moving our bodies and refreshing ourselves, we maintain the team’s concentration and the quality of our work.

  • Relieving stiff shoulders
  • Improving posture

Frequency and Timing #

  • Optional (e.g., every day after lunch break)

How to Run It #

  • The whole team does Radio Taiso together while playing a video on a site such as YouTube

References

  • Radio Taiso No. 1 (YouTube)
